mcqs.question: A book is lying on a table. Which statement correctly explains why it remains at rest?

options.A: A continuous upward force is acting on the book to keep it stationary.
options.B: No net external force acts on the book, so its state of rest is maintained.
options.C: Gravity constantly pushes the book forward.
options.D: Friction constantly pulls the book backward.

mcqs.answer: No net external force acts on the book, so its state of rest is maintained.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of rest means an object at rest stays at rest unless a net external force acts on it. Here gravity is balanced by the normal reaction, giving zero net force, so the book remains where it is. Option B states this correctly; the other options describe forces that are not present or misinterpret the situation.

mcqs.question: A soccer ball rolls on a smooth field and gradually comes to a stop. Which reasoning best explains this observation?

options.A: The ball’s inertia disappears over time.
options.B: External forces such as friction act opposite to its motion, reducing its speed.
options.C: Inertia causes moving objects to stop automatically.
options.D: Gravity pulls the ball downward, making it stop.

mcqs.answer: External forces such as friction act opposite to its motion, reducing its speed.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion states that a moving object continues in motion unless acted upon by a net external force. The ball slows because friction (and possibly air resistance) provides a force opposite to its motion, removing kinetic energy. Option B captures this; the other options either deny inertia or attribute stopping to unrelated forces.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly compares inertia of direction with inertia of rest?

options.A: Inertia of direction resists changes in speed, while inertia of rest resists changes in direction.
options.B: Inertia of direction resists a change in the direction of motion, whereas inertia of rest resists a change from rest to motion.
options.C: Both refer to the same property of mass and are indistinguishable.
options.D: Inertia of direction applies only to rotating bodies, while inertia of rest applies to linear motion.

mcqs.answer: Inertia of direction resists a change in the direction of motion, whereas inertia of rest resists a change from rest to motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of direction (sometimes called inertia of motion) opposes any change in the direction of a moving object, while inertia of rest opposes the initiation of motion from a stationary state. Option B states this distinction accurately; the other options mix up the concepts or add incorrect restrictions.

mcqs.question: Which everyday situation best illustrates the inertia of direction?

options.A: A passenger lurches forward when a car suddenly stops.
options.B: A cup remains stationary on a table.
options.C: A ball rolls down an inclined plane.
options.D: A kite flies steadily in a constant wind.

mcqs.answer: A passenger lurches forward when a car suddenly stops.
mcqs.explanation: When the car stops abruptly, the passenger’s body tends to continue moving in the original direction due to inertia of direction, causing them to lurch forward. This is a classic example used in competitive exams. The other options illustrate inertia of rest or motion, not direction.

mcqs.question: In physics, inertia is defined as:

options.A: The tendency of an object to accelerate when a force is applied.
options.B: The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.
options.C: The force required to move an object.
options.D: The speed of an object in motion.

mcqs.answer: The tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is the property of matter that resists changes in its motion, whether the object is at rest or moving. Option B gives the textbook definition; the other options describe unrelated concepts such as acceleration, required force, or speed.

mcqs.question: If a cup is placed on a table and left untouched, why does it stay where it is?

options.A: Because of its inertia of rest, which resists any change in motion.

mcqs.answer: Because of its inertia of rest, which resists any change in motion.
mcqs.explanation: The cup remains at rest because, in the absence of a net external force, its inertia of rest keeps it stationary. Gravity is balanced by the normal force, so there is no net vertical force causing motion. Options B, C, and D are either irrelevant or incorrect.

mcqs.question: How does inertia of motion differ from inertia of rest?

options.A: Inertia of motion resists a change in speed or direction of a moving object, whereas inertia of rest resists the start of motion of a stationary object.
options.B: Inertia of motion causes objects to stop, while inertia of rest causes them to start moving.
options.C: Both are identical and refer to the same phenomenon.
options.D: Inertia of motion only applies to liquids, whereas inertia of rest applies to solids.

mcqs.answer: Inertia of motion resists a change in speed or direction of a moving object, whereas inertia of rest resists the start of motion of a stationary object.
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion (also called inertia of direction) opposes changes in the velocity (speed or direction) of a moving body, while inertia of rest opposes the initiation of motion from rest. Option A captures this distinction; the other options are misconceptions.

mcqs.question: A ball moving in a straight line hits a wall and bounces back. Which aspect of inertia is demonstrated?

options.A: Inertia of direction, resisting change in direction.

mcqs.answer: Inertia of direction, resisting change in direction.
mcqs.explanation: When the ball hits the wall, its direction changes sharply. The tendency of the ball to continue in its original direction illustrates inertia of direction. Option A correctly identifies this; the other options do not apply to the scenario.
